title: IG Metall calls 24-hour warning strikes in northern Germany

tea.why: Protesters are striking over stalled collective bargaining negotiations and wage disputes in the metal and electrical industries.
tea.want: Protesters demand a 5% wage increase alongside guarantees for job and plant security.
tea.changed: Nov 22: IG Metall announced a 24-hour warning strike involving over 23,000 workers across 19 northern German companies starting Monday.

summary: The trade union IG Metall has called for a 24-hour warning strike starting Monday across northern Germany, involving over 23,000 workers at 19 enterprises including Mercedes-Benz, Meyer Werft, and Siemens Gamesa. According to sources, the industrial action is an escalation of a pay dispute after three rounds of negotiations failed to yield an agreement. The union is demanding a 5% wage increase and job security guarantees, while employers have proposed delaying permanent wage hikes for 20 months with a 1.3% increase starting in July 2028.
response: Employers proposed a one-time payment in July 2027 and a 1.3 percent structural wage increase starting in July 2028, citing high costs and weak demand.

updates.text: IG Metall announced a 24-hour warning strike involving over 23,000 workers across 19 companies in northern Germany.
